Description:en: An offensive, foul breath odor resulting from a variety of causes such as poor oral hygiene, dental or oral infections, or the ingestion of certain foods.
Is the release of air from the stomach through the mouth
Snapping jaw is a condition in which a person experiences a clicking, popping, or snapping sound or sensation in the jaw when opening or closing the mouth, chewing, or yawning.
Is a condition where the mouth feels dry due to reduced saliva production or changes in saliva flow.

Spasmodic contraction of the masseter muscle resulting in forceful jaw closure. This may be seen with a variety of diseases, including TETANUS, as a complication of radiation therapy, trauma, or in association with neoplastic conditions.
Pain in the adjacent areas of the teeth.

An oral habit consisting of involuntary rhythmic or spasmodic nonfunctional gnashing, grinding, and clenching of teeth on other than chewing movements of the mandible, usually performed during sleep, which may lead to occlusal trauma. Causes are believed to be related to repressed aggression, emotional tension, anger, fear, and frustration. (Dorland, 27th ed)
Is a sharp, short pain or discomfort in one or more teeth when exposed to cold, hot, sweet, sour, or air.
Question which ascertains number of symptoms related to a person's dental health.
Progressive loss of the hard substance of a tooth by chemical processes that do not involve bacterial action. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p296)
teeth that fail to fully erupt into their normal position in the mouth because they are blocked by bone, gum tissue, or other teeth.

Such malposition and contact of the maxillary and mandibular teeth as to interfere with the highest efficiency during the excursive movements of the jaw that are essential for mastication. (Jablonski, Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982)
A film that attaches to teeth, often causing DENTAL CARIES and GINGIVITIS. It is composed of MUCINS, secreted from salivary glands, and microorganisms.

Acute or chronic inflammation of tissues surrounding the apical portion of a tooth, associated with the collection of pus, resulting from infection following pulp infection through a carious lesion or as a result of an injury causing pulp necrosis. (Dorland, 27th ed)

A variety of conditions affecting the anatomic and functional characteristics of the temporomandibular joint. Factors contributing to the complexity of temporomandibular diseases are its relation to dentition and mastication and the symptomatic effects in other areas which account for referred pain to the joint and the difficulties in applying traditional diagnostic procedures to temporomandibular joint pathology where tissue is rarely obtained and x-rays are often inadequate or nonspecific. Common diseases are developmental abnormalities, trauma, subluxation, luxation, arthritis, and neoplasia. (From Thoma's Oral Pathology, 6th ed, pp577-600)
Categorization of diagnosis
Procedure to extract the molar tooth
A dental procedure involving the release or removal of an impacted tooth using a closed surgical approach.
A dental surgical procedure involving the exposure and release of an impacted tooth through an open surgical approach to facilitate its eruption or removal.
A dental procedure involving the assessment, irrigation, pain management, and application of medicated dressings when indicated to treat dry socket (alveolar osteitis) following tooth extraction.
A procedure involving the realignment and stabilization of fractured mandibular bone segments without surgically exposing the fracture site.
A surgical procedure involving direct exposure and realignment of fractured mandibular bone segments, followed by stabilization using internal fixation devices such as plates and screws.

A dental surgical procedure involving the removal of excess gum tissue (operculum) covering a partially erupted tooth to expose the tooth crown and facilitate normal eruption, improve oral hygiene, or prevent recurrent inflammation and infection.
Surgical removal of a frenum that restricts movement of the tongue or lip or interferes with oral function.
Surgical removal of the tip of a tooth root to treat persistent disease around the root apex.
Stabilization of teeth by linking them to adjacent teeth or supporting them with a splint.
Surgical reshaping and smoothing of the alveolar ridge, often after extractions or before fitting a denture.
Collection of cells from an oral lesion with a brush for laboratory examination.
Measurement of the volume of stimulated or unstimulated saliva produced over a timed interval.
Restoration of a prepared tooth cavity with dental amalgam.
Restoration of lost or damaged tooth structure with tooth-colored composite resin.
Repair or replacement of lost tooth structure using a polyacid-modified composite resin.
Restoration of lost tooth structure using glass ionomer cement.
Restoration of a small carious area with composite resin and sealing of adjacent susceptible pits and fissures.
Placement of a protective material directly over exposed vital dental pulp to preserve pulp vitality.
Reconstruction of lost tooth structure using small pins anchored in dentin to retain the restorative material.
Lightening of natural teeth using a chemical bleaching agent.
In-office tooth whitening using a concentrated bleaching agent under professional supervision.
Controlled removal of a thin layer of enamel with an acid-abrasive agent to reduce superficial discoloration or defects.
Application and shaping of composite resin directly on the front surface of a tooth to improve its appearance.
Bonding of a composite resin veneer fabricated outside the mouth to the front surface of a tooth.
Bonding of a thin porcelain facing to a tooth to improve its color, shape, or surface appearance.
Concealment of tooth discoloration or an aesthetic defect with a tooth-colored material.
Placement of a prefabricated post in a root-treated tooth and construction of a core to support a crown.
Placement of a custom-cast post and core in a root-treated tooth to provide support for a crown.
Restoration of damaged teeth or replacement of missing teeth with fixed crowns or bridges.
Provision of a fixed dental restoration made with zirconia to restore or replace teeth.
Cementation or bonding of an indirectly fabricated restoration within a prepared tooth cavity.
Cementation or bonding of an indirectly fabricated restoration that covers one or more tooth cusps.
Reattachment of an existing crown or bridge to its supporting tooth or abutment using dental cement.
Reattachment of an existing complex fixed bridge to its supporting abutments using dental cement.
Removal of an existing crown or fixed bridge from its supporting teeth or abutments.
Repair of chipped, fractured, or otherwise damaged porcelain on an existing dental restoration.
Repair of a fractured denture to restore its integrity and function.
Addition of a prosthetic tooth to an existing denture to replace a missing tooth.
Provision of complete removable dentures to replace all teeth in both dental arches.
Provision of a complete removable denture to replace all teeth in one dental arch.
Provision of a removable acrylic partial denture to replace one to three missing teeth.
Provision of a removable acrylic partial denture to replace four to six missing teeth.

Fully specified name:en: ACRYLIC PARTIAL DENTURE (7 OR MORE TEETH)
Description:en: Provision of a removable acrylic partial denture to replace seven or more missing teeth.
Provision of a removable partial denture supported by a cobalt-chromium alloy framework.

Fully specified name:en: REPAIR OF COBALT CHROME DENTURE FRAMEWORK
Description:en: Repair of a damaged cobalt-chromium framework in an existing removable partial denture.
Provision of a hard, full-coverage stabilization splint that provides controlled contacts with the opposing teeth.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF DENTAL MOUTHGUARD.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of an appliance that protects the teeth and surrounding tissues from injury.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF ACRYLIC OBTURATOR PROSTHESIS
Description:en: Construction and fitting of an acrylic prosthesis that closes a palatal or maxillary defect.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF COBALT-CHROMIUM OBTURATOR PROSTHESIS.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of a prosthesis with a cobalt-chromium framework to close a palatal or maxillary defect.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF FACIAL PROSTHESIS
Description:en: Construction and fitting of a custom external prosthesis to replace a missing facial structure.
Professional cleaning to remove plaque, calculus, and surface stains as part of preventive dental care.
Filling of a prepared tooth cavity with a compomer, a polyacid-modified resin-based material.
Removal of part or all of the coronal dental pulp while preserving the pulp in the roots.
Application of a protective material to tooth pits and fissures to reduce the risk of dental caries.

Fully specified name:en: PLACEMENT OF STAINLESS STEEL DENTAL CROWN
Description:en: Fitting and cementation of a preformed stainless steel crown to provide full coverage of a tooth.
Placement of a fixed bridge retained by adhesive bonding to the supporting teeth.
Production of models of the dental arches for orthodontic assessment and treatment planning.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF INITIAL REMOVABLE ORTHODONTIC APPLIANCE.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of the first removable appliance prescribed in a course of orthodontic treatment.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF SECOND REMOVABLE ORTHODONTIC APPLIANCE.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of a second removable appliance during the same course of orthodontic treatment.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF REMOVABLE ORTHODONTIC HABIT-BREAKING APPLIANCE.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of a removable appliance designed to interrupt a persistent oral habit.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF REMOVABLE ORTHODONTIC RETAINER
Description:en: Construction and fitting of a removable appliance that maintains tooth position after orthodontic movement.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF REMOVABLE DENTAL SPACE MAINTAINER.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of a removable appliance that preserves space after premature loss of a tooth.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF FIXED ORTHODONTIC HABIT-BREAKING APPLIANCE.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of an appliance secured to the teeth to interrupt a persistent oral habit.
Bonding of a retaining appliance to the teeth to maintain their positions after orthodontic movement.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND PLACEMENT OF FIXED DENTAL SPACE MAINTAINER.
Description:en: Construction and attachment of an appliance to preserve space after premature tooth loss.
Correction of tooth position or bite using orthodontic appliances secured to the teeth.

Fully specified name:en: PLACEMENT OF SECTIONAL FIXED ORTHODONTIC APPLIANCE.
Description:en: Attachment of a fixed orthodontic appliance to a limited segment of the dental arch for localized tooth movement.

Fully specified name:en: FABRICATION AND FITTING OF REMOVABLE ORTHODONTIC APPLIANCE WITH EXPANSION SCREW.
Description:en: Construction and fitting of a removable appliance with an adjustable screw for gradual dental arch expansion.

Fully specified name:en: PLACEMENT OF BAND AND LOOP SPACE MAINTAINER.
Description:en: Attachment of a band to a supporting tooth with a loop that preserves the space left by a missing tooth.
Repair of a damaged orthodontic appliance to restore its prescribed function.
Preventive cleaning that includes polishing tooth surfaces to remove surface stains and deposits.
Removal of plaque and calculus from tooth surfaces throughout both dental arches.
Removal of inflamed soft tissue from the lining of a periodontal pocket with a curette.
Surgical reflection of gingival tissue to access and treat affected root surfaces or supporting bone.
Use of the patient's own bone and a barrier membrane to promote bone formation at a deficient site.
Use of donor bone from another person and a barrier membrane to promote bone formation at a deficient site.
Surgical excision of gingival tissue to remove excess tissue or reduce periodontal pockets.
Surgical reshaping of the gingiva to improve its contour around the teeth.
Surgical exposure of additional tooth structure by repositioning or removing gingiva, with bone reshaping when needed.
Placement of a soft-tissue graft to augment gingiva or cover an exposed tooth root.
Surgical removal of one root of a multirooted tooth while retaining the remaining portion of the tooth.
Surgical removal of a representative portion of an oral lesion for histopathological examination.
Surgical removal of an entire oral lesion for histopathological examination.
Surgical removal of the gingival flap covering part of a partially erupted tooth.
Placement of a barrier membrane to favor regeneration of periodontal attachment and supporting tissues.

Fully specified name:en: DENTAL BONE GRAFTING WITH BARRIER MEMBRANE
Description:en: Placement of bone graft material and a protective membrane to rebuild bone at a dental site.
Application of fluoride directly to tooth surfaces to strengthen enamel against acid attack and help prevent caries.
Stabilization of mobile teeth by joining them to one another or to adjacent teeth to limit movement.

Fully specified name:en: PLACEMENT OF SINGLE OSSEOINTEGRATED DENTAL IMPLANT
Description:en: Surgical insertion of one dental implant into jawbone for integration with the bone and future prosthetic support.
Surgical placement of a second dental implant in the same jaw during the same procedure.
Surgical placement of a third dental implant in the same jaw during the same procedure.
Surgical uncovering of one previously placed implant to allow access for placement of a healing abutment or prosthetic component.
Surgical uncovering of a second previously placed implant in the same jaw.
Surgical uncovering of a third previously placed implant in the same jaw.
Surgical removal of a wedge of excess gingival tissue behind the last tooth in an arch to reduce a periodontal pocket.
